**Finding submitted: MISSING (INSURANCE)**

**What I found:** The Agreement is a single-section MSA (p0000–p0074). A literal search for "insurance" returns zero hits, and a full read confirms there is no insurance covenant anywhere — no CGL, no professional liability/E&O, no cyber/privacy, no workers' compensation, and no certificate-of-insurance or additional-insured mechanic.

**Why the rule applies:** Kubient is a services/hosting vendor that touches our data. Its own warranty at p0035 covers "the collection, maintenance, management and storage of visitor information (data)... collected, directed by, maintained or stored by Kubient," and it is a Recipient of our Confidential Information under Section 12. A data-processing vendor with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under the rule, not a fallback-level clause — so this is a genuine gap rather than a minor sub-element.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** Inserted a new General Provisions subsection (j) after p0073 — the natural miscellaneous location, immediately before the signature block — at the preferred position: CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M, workers' compensation as required by law, certificates on request, held through the Term plus one year. The comment flags the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) as a negotiation path if Kubient pushes back on the cyber limit.

One drafting note: I used "the Term" (a defined term at p0016) rather than the model language's generic "the term," and framed the covenant on "Kubient" rather than "Vendor" to match the document's naming convention.
